"""Query-string delimiters in web addresses and key=value strings, plus two small
recurring cases.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:896 is strongly negative on the characters that
open and continue a URL's query string: the "?" that starts the query (also "?q",
"?v") after a web path or domain, and the "&" between key=value pairs (also "&q",
"&per"). Elsewhere it is near zero: "?" in questions, "&&" in shell commands,
HTML entities such as "'", and "&" in maths or code.

Two smaller recurring cases: the " b" of a git diff header ("+++ b/...") is negative,
and the "field" of a place name (Bradfield, Chesterfield) is positive.

The program tracks the current whitespace-delimited word and the previous token.
A "?" that starts a token gets a strong negative value when that word looks like a
web path or domain (a letter before a "/", a dotted domain ending, "://" or "www.").
A bare "&" gets a weaker negative value when the word so far has a "key=" in it.
Words containing maths symbols are skipped. Anything else is 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

MATH_CHARS = "*^{}$\\≈"
PATH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]/[A-Za-z]|\.(com|org|net|io|edu|gov|html?|php|aspx?|do|jsp|cgi|jpg|png)|://|www\.")
Q_VALUE = -6.0     # "?" that starts a query string after a path or domain
AMP_VALUE = -4.5   # "&" between key=value pairs
DIFF_B = -2.0      # " b" in "+++ b/path" of a git diff
FIELD = 1.7        # "field" ending a place name


def is_param_start(s, mark):
    """A token that is the bare mark, or the mark followed by a letter or digit ("?q", "&page")."""
    return s == mark or (s.startswith(mark) and s[1:].isalnum())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word, prev = "", ""
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        word, prev = carry[1], carry[2]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if not any(c in word for c in MATH_CHARS):
        if is_param_start(s, "?"):
            if PATH.search(word):
                value = Q_VALUE
        elif is_param_start(s, "&") and "=" in word:
            value = AMP_VALUE
    if value == 0.0:
        if s == " b" and prev == "+++":
            value = DIFF_B
        elif s == "field" and word[-1:].isalpha():
            value = FIELD

    # extend the current word; whitespace starts a new one
    word = word + s
    cut = max(word.rfind(c) for c in " \t\n\r")
    word = word[cut + 1:][-200:]
    return (doc, word, s), value

"""A partial lexical approximation to physical/biological mechanism language.

Join English word pieces and score familiar scientific and process word families.
A fading scientific-vocabulary context boosts some families, especially systems,
transport, mechanisms, and causation. Clinical descriptions pull the other way.
Also model negative offsets at document starts and thinking markers. This does
not capture the component's many word-specific or non-English effects.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import NamedTuple

READS = ()


class Family(NamedTuple):
    name: str
    roots: str
    current: float
    previous: float
    context_gain: float
    of_complement: float


# Each row has one shared score per human-readable word family, not per token.
FAMILIES = (
    Family(
        'energy',
        'energy energet heat thermal electric power force radiat wave '
        'photon',
        0.163, 0.068, 0.063, -0.059,
    ),
    Family(
        'chemical',
        'chem molecul atom bond acid hydro oxid ioniz enzyme cataly '
        'protein amino',
        0.259, 0.024, -0.023, 0.257,
    ),
    Family(
        'cellular',
        'cell membran vascular vessel cyto plasma lymph neuro axon '
        'organell reticul mitochond',
        0.323, 0.048, 0.332, 0.151,
    ),
    Family(
        'biological',
        'bio physio metabol gene genet immun hormon receptor blood tissue '
        'muscl nerv',
        0.073, 0.051, -0.136, 0.081,
    ),
    Family(
        'formation',
        'form produc generat creat synthes origin develop growth grow',
        0.091, -0.003, 0.165, 0.242,
    ),
    Family(
        'dynamics',
        'flow transport transfer releas absorb emiss diffus circul motion '
        'move migrat',
        0.192, 0.062, 0.38, 0.217,
    ),
    Family(
        'mechanism',
        'activ react interact bind coupl signal regulat feedback mechanis '
        'function process pathway circuit',
        0.143, 0.033, 0.525, 0.26,
    ),
    Family(
        'causal',
        'caus effect result respons role involv induc contribut lead '
        'trigger allow enable convert exert',
        0.051, 0.023, 0.39, 0.101,
    ),
    Family(
        'change',
        'increas decreas reduc enhanc inhibit suppress accumul degrad '
        'decay loss gain transfor',
        0.107, 0.045, 0.137, 0.191,
    ),
    Family(
        'structure',
        'structur system unit layer wall site network chain complex '
        'assembl loop',
        0.07, 0.004, 0.346, 0.117,
    ),
    Family(
        'clinical',
        'disease disorder cancer tumor treat therap diagnos patient '
        'symptom syndrome',
        -0.113, 0.029, -0.342, -0.135,
    ),
    Family(
        'measurement',
        'measur temperatur observ stud experiment research test analysis',
        -0.005, 0.002, -0.137, -0.026,
    ),
)
SCIENTIFIC = {'energy', 'chemical', 'cellular', 'biological'}


@lru_cache(maxsize=30000)
def families(word):
    return tuple(f for f in FAMILIES
                 if any(word.startswith(root) for root in f.roots.split()))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    reset = carry is None or (len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and
                             prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2])
    fragment, previous, last, context = ('', '', '', 0.) if reset else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    words = re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', token.lower())
    continued = bool(fragment and token[:1].isascii() and token[:1].isalpha())
    if words:
        if continued:
            words[0] = fragment + words[0]
        word = words[-1]
        previous = previous if continued and len(words) == 1 else last
        if len(words) > 1:
            previous = words[-2]
        last = word
        fragment = word if token[-1:].isascii() and token[-1:].isalpha() else ''
    else:
        word, fragment, previous = '', '', last
    current, before = families(word), families(previous)
    value = 0.005 + 0.089 * context
    value += 0.026 * continued + -0.006 * bool(word)
    for family in current:
        value += family.current + context * family.context_gain
    for family in before:
        value += family.previous
        if word == 'of':
            value += family.of_complement
    if word.endswith(('ation', 'ations', 'ization', 'isation')):
        value += 0.05
    if word.endswith(('ase', 'ases')):
        value += 0.011
    if word.endswith(('ose', 'oses')):
        value += 0.016
    if word.endswith(('ide', 'ides', 'ate', 'ates', 'ine', 'ines')):
        value += 0.026
    value += -0.006 * token.isspace()
    value += -0.002 * token.strip().isdigit()
    if token.strip() and not words and not token.strip().isalnum():
        value += -0.006
    value += 0.003 * token.startswith('<|')
    value += -0.356 * reset
    value += -0.18 * (token in ('<think>', '</think>'))
    value += -0.043 * (token == '<|im_start|>')
    technical = any(f.name in SCIENTIFIC for f in current + before)
    context = .85 * context + .15 * technical
    return (fragment, previous, last, context), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:897: a 'biology register' detector, written as a readable program.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It is positive on cell-biology, biochemistry and physiology words (cells, glucose, ATP, ROS,
  receptor, pathway, secretion, flow, energy, ...), and it is positive for the function words
  and content words that follow them when a passage is dense in such vocabulary.
- It is negative on disease and clinical words (disease, infection, virus, patients, ...).
- The first token of every document is a fixed dip (about -0.36): with no context before it,
  the component reads as negative.

It tracks a running density of biology and disease words in the current document (an
exponential average over earlier tokens, reset at each document start) and adds it to the
token-level terms. The coefficients are least-squares fits to the component's activation on
2048 training rows; on the eval rows the program explains about 3.5% of the variance (r = 0.19), which
is far below a full per-token table (about 15% on held-out rows): most of the variance is in
word-specific detail that a short word list cannot carry. Switching the component off, or
using this program, changes the model's next-token distribution almost identically.
"""
READS = ()

BIO = set("""
cell cells cellular protein proteins enzyme enzymes gene genes dna rna mrna atp adp glucose
sugar oxygen hormone hormones receptor receptors binding bind signaling signal pathway pathways
metabolism metabolic molecule molecules synthesis transcription replication regulation regulate
regulatory secretion secrete release membrane nucleus mitochondria mitochondrial ros oxidative
oxidation calcium ca ion ions proton ph acid tissue tissues organ organs neurons neuron muscle
muscles blood vessels vessel flow energy process processes mechanism mechanisms activation
activate activates contraction stimulus transport absorption cortisol glucose
""".split())

DISEASE = set("""
disease diseases infection infections virus viruses influenza syndrome disorder disorders
treatment treating treated screening diagnosis patients antibody antibodies bacteria
bacterial species humans diet natural supplement
""".split())

DECAY = 0.95              # how quickly the running density forgets earlier words
DOC_START = -0.36         # the first token of a document
BIO_WORD = 0.25           # a biology word
DIS_WORD = -0.29          # a disease word
BIO_DENSITY = 1.08        # every token, scaled by the biology density before it
DIS_DENSITY = 0.27        # every token, scaled by the disease density before it
BIO_WORD_IN_DENSITY = 1.54  # extra push for a biology word inside a biology-dense passage


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    bio, dis = (0.0, 0.0) if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    is_bio = word in BIO
    is_dis = word in DISEASE
    value = BIO_DENSITY * bio + DIS_DENSITY * dis
    if is_bio:
        value += BIO_WORD + BIO_WORD_IN_DENSITY * bio
    if is_dis:
        value += DIS_WORD
    if new_doc:
        value += DOC_START
    bio = DECAY * bio + (1 - DECAY) * is_bio
    dis = DECAY * dis + (1 - DECAY) * is_dis
    return (bio, dis), value

programs.sol:
"""An approximate nominalized-action detector.

A singular-looking action/process noun with a noun-forming ending gets a
positive signal, stronger after a determiner and much stronger on a following 'of' (or
another genitive linker). Romance and Slavic nominal endings are recognized too.
Dictionary process nouns also get a signal in noun contexts. Other tokens are
near zero. Action nouns often introduce an object with 'of', so the noun cue
is reused at that linker. Word-specific strengths and richer syntax are omitted.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
DETERMINERS = set(('the a an this that these those its their his her our '
                    'your my any some each every no').split())
LINKERS = set('of de di du del da do des der'.split())
NOMINAL = re.compile(r'(?:tion|sion|ment|ance|ence|ure|age|al|ing)$')
ROMANCE = re.compile(
    r'(?:ción|sión|ção|ções|zioni|zione|amento|imento|amiento|imiento|'
    r'area|irea|ement|issement)$')
SLAVIC = re.compile(
    r'(?:ение|ения|ении|ению|ание|ания|ании|анию|аня|ння|'
    r'owanie|owania|aniu|enie|ением)$')

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def noun_classes(word):
    return wordnet.categories(word, 'noun')


def response(word, before, linker, continued):
    classes = noun_classes(word)
    process = 'noun.process' in classes
    action = process or 'noun.act' in classes
    determiner = before in DETERMINERS
    if action and NOMINAL.search(word) and not word.endswith('s'):
        if linker:
            prior_noun = 'noun' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(before)
            return 0.74 if prior_noun else 1.58
        return 0.43 if determiner else 0.075
    if SLAVIC.search(word):
        return 1.28
    if not classes and ROMANCE.search(word):
        if linker:
            return 0.79
        if continued:
            return 0.63
    if linker:
        return 0.83 if process else 0.095
    if process and determiner:
        return 0.62
    return 0.003


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    continued = bool(tail and tail[-1].isalpha() and token
                     and token[0].isalpha())
    text = (tail + token)[-180:]
    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', text)
    if not text or not text[-1].isalpha() or not words:
        return (doc, text), 0.003
    linker = words[-1].lower() in LINKERS
    j = -2 if linker else -1
    word = words[j].lower() if len(words) >= -j else ''
    before = words[j-1].lower() if len(words) >= 1-j else ''
    return (doc, text), response(word, before, linker, continued)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:898 -- fires on "of" after an event (process/action) noun.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is a "nominalisation complement" detector.
When a word names an event or process that acts on something (the transfer OF, the
development OF, the election OF, the signing OF, the use OF), the next word is very
likely the complement "of" (or its foreign equivalents de / von / di / del / do / van).
The component writes a large positive value onto that linking word. The strength
depends on the words around it:

- a list of event nouns gives the strongest response; an event-like ending
  (-tion, -sion, -ment, -ing) on a word not in NOT_EVENTS gives a somewhat weaker one;
- "the X of" is stronger than a bare "X of" (about 1.7x), and "a X of" is weak
  (about 0.15x), since "a sale of" is rare for the component;
- the event noun itself fires a little (0.15), and nominal endings used in other
  languages (Russian -ение/-ения, German -ung, Portuguese -ção, Spanish -ación)
  fire on their own at about 0.8.

Everything else predicts 0. Most of the component's variance is small, diffuse noise
on ordinary tokens that no short rule captures, so this program explains the large
events only.
"""

# Event / process nouns: things that happen or are done to something.
EVENT_NOUNS = set("""
acquisition addition administration advancement analysis application approval assembly
assessment birth breakdown breach change collapse collection combination completion comparison
conduct construction consumption control creation death decrease delivery design destruction
development diagnosis disclosure discovery dispensing disposal distribution elimination
election emergence employment enforcement establishment evaluation exchange execution
exercise expansion expression extraction fall flow formation generation growth handling
implementation improvement increase induction installation integration introduction killing
lack launch loss maintenance making management manufacturing measurement migration movement
murder onset operation outbreak payment performance practice preparation presence processing
production provision provisions purchase recruitment reduction release removal rise repair
replacement return rollout sale security selection spread start study success supply support
synthesis transfer transmission transport treatment unveiling use usage utilization
adoption alteration amendment appointment arrangement arrival attack avoidance cancellation
classification computation configuration confirmation connection conservation consideration
contraction conversion cooperation coordination correction deployment deposition derivation
description detection determination deviation digestion discharge dismissal division donation
drainage encouragement engagement enhancement entry estimation examination exploitation
exploration exposure fabrication identification importation impairment incorporation infection
inflation infusion inhibition initiation injection inspection interpretation investigation
invasion isolation labeling legislation liberation limitation loading manipulation manufacture
mediation modification monitoring nomination observation optimization organization overhaul
perception placement planning prescription prevention promotion protection publication
reception recognition recording recovery reform refusal regulation rejection relaxation
rendering reorganization reproduction request rescue research reservation resolution
restoration restriction retention revelation review revision revolution scanning separation
settlement shipment sharing simulation sorting specification stimulation subtraction
substitution suppression suspension termination testing training transformation validation
variation verification visualization withdrawal writing survival pruning appearance departure
decline recession erosion worship pathogenesis
""".split())

# Nouns that end like events (-tion, -ment, -ing) but name things, parts or amounts.
NOT_EVENTS = set("""
section portion version region population function department element fraction segment
condition question information meaning duration government union fragment statement
embodiment moment proportion opinion environment dimension tradition religion decision
position collection location station nation king thing string something nothing everything
part member percent because ratio period factors form terms majority rest half matter number
range variety couple lot kind type one none both either all some most many sort way front end
""".split())

EVENT_ENDINGS = ("tion", "sion", "ment", "ing")
# Nominal endings of event nouns in other languages (Russian, German, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian).
FOREIGN_ENDINGS = (
    "ение", "ения", "ении", "ание", "ания", "ании",  # Russian
    "ung", "ção", "ación", "azione",
)
LINKERS = (" of", " de", " von", " di", " del", " do", " van")

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    pieces = prefix.token_strings
    cur = pieces[-1]
    if cur.endswith(FOREIGN_ENDINGS):
        return None, 0.8  # a foreign event-noun ending, on its own
    if cur.strip().lower() in EVENT_NOUNS:
        return None, 0.15  # the event noun itself, a little
    if cur not in LINKERS:
        return None, 0.0

    # Walk back over the word before the linker, and note the token before that word.
    i = len(pieces) - 2
    word = ""
    while i >= 0:
        piece = pieces[i]
        word = piece + word
        if piece[:1] == " " or not piece.strip():
            break
        i -= 1
    word = word.strip().lower()
    before = pieces[i - 1].strip().lower() if i >= 1 else ""

    if word in NOT_EVENTS:
        return None, 0.0
    if word in EVENT_NOUNS:
        strength = 1.1
    elif word.endswith(EVENT_ENDINGS) or word.endswith(FOREIGN_ENDINGS):
        strength = 0.9
    else:
        return None, 0.0
    if before in ("a", "an"):
        strength *= 0.15
    elif before == "the":
        strength *= 1.7
    return None, strength

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 899: a sparse, mostly silent feature.

On almost every token it is near zero. It is large (either sign) on two kinds of token:

1. A colon right after the word "Title" (boilerplate such as "<|endoftext|>Title: ..."),
   where it is strongly negative.
2. A later piece of a word that is split across tokens, when the piece is made of letters
   and joins a letter-only piece in the same document (e.g. "she" + "af" in "sheaf",
   "Math" + "ematic"). The sign and size depend on which piece it is, so only a few of the
   most consistent pieces are listed.

Everywhere else it predicts 0. The predicted values are averages over sampled text.
"""

READS = ()

# Word pieces that finish a split word, with their typical activation.
FRAGMENT_VALUES = {
    "ematic": -4.0,
    "het": -2.0,
    "thal": -0.6,
    "ät": -0.4,
    "ash": -0.2,
    "hash": 1.9,
    "Hash": 0.5,
    "ather": 1.2,
    "ham": 0.3,
    "cal": 0.2,
    "bf": 0.2,
    "heit": 0.2,
    "hev": 0.3,
    "하": 0.3,
    "학": 0.4,
}
TITLE_COLON_VALUE = -2.3


def _is_letters(text):
    return len(text) > 0 and text.isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    cur = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if t == 0:
        return None, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[t - 1]
    same_doc = prefix.document_ids[t] == prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    if not same_doc:
        return None, 0.0
    if cur == ":" and prev == "Title":
        return None, TITLE_COLON_VALUE
    fragment = (
        not cur.startswith(" ")
        and not prev.startswith(" ")
        and _is_letters(cur)
        and _is_letters(prev)
    )
    if fragment and cur in FRAGMENT_VALUES:
        return None, FRAGMENT_VALUES[cur]
    return None, 0.0

"""Thousands-separator zeros: layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 900.

What it does
    The component is quiet almost everywhere, but it lights up on the digits that open the
    thousands group of a number written with commas. Its strongest case is the first "0"
    straight after a comma in a number of two or three digits, as in "$100,|0|00",
    "2,|0|00" or "272,|0|00": the model has read "...X," and the next digit is a 0, which
    starts a ",000" group. A second 0 in the same group ("272,0|0|0") fires too, less.
    Non-zero first digits after a comma fire weakly ("$133,|1|25"). A bare comma after a
    number is a little positive (it is what precedes the group). Everything else is near 0.

    It is weaker in data-like text (decimals, coordinate tuples, CSV rows such as
    "0.12,0.25,0.0") and somewhat stronger in running prose, so the program scales the
    digit values down after ".", ",", "(", "=" or "/", and up after a space, "$" or a word.

Why this is a readable concept
    "Digit that starts or continues a thousands group after a comma" is a plain
    typographic idea. The program only needs the digit count before the comma, whether the
    digit is 0, and what precedes the number.

How it is scored
    Its predictions explain about half the variance of the component's activation on
    training rows. The rest is spread over many tokens and magnitudes that are hard to
    summarise simply (the size of the number and how prose-like the text is).

Main program: `step` returns this position's predicted activation from the tokens so far.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789")

# Predicted activation of the first digit after a comma, by the number of digits before the
# comma (1, 2, 3 or more), when that digit is 0 and when it is not.
FIRST_ZERO = {1: 2.5, 2: 7.7}
FIRST_ZERO_LONG = 5.7
FIRST_OTHER = {1: 1.2, 2: 2.8}
FIRST_OTHER_LONG = 3.0
# Second digit of the group: after a 0 as first digit, and after a non-zero first digit.
SECOND_AFTER_ZERO = (3.5, 0.9)  # (if this digit is 0, if not)
SECOND_AFTER_OTHER = (1.2, 0.6)
# A bare comma right after a number, by how many digits the number has.
COMMA_AFTER = {1: 0.2, 2: 0.7, 3: 0.9}

DATA_LIKE = frozenset(".,(=/")  # the token before the number: decimals, tuples, code
PROSE_LIKE = frozenset(" $\xa0")


def _run_back(strings, i):
    """How many digit tokens end at index i, and the index just before them."""
    n = 0
    while i >= 0 and strings[i] in DIGITS:
        n += 1
        i -= 1
    return n, i


def _is_word(text):
    return text.strip()[:1].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    t = len(s) - 1
    if t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return None, 0.0  # a new document starts here: no number runs across it
    tok = s[t]
    value = 0.0
    if tok == ",":
        digits_before, _ = _run_back(s, t - 1)
        value = COMMA_AFTER.get(digits_before, 0.0)
    elif tok in DIGITS:
        in_group, j = _run_back(s, t - 1)  # digits already after the comma, in this group
        if in_group <= 1 and j >= 0 and s[j] == ",":
            number_len, i = _run_back(s, j - 1)  # digits of the number before the comma
            if number_len >= 1:
                zero = tok == "0"
                if in_group == 0:
                    if zero:
                        value = FIRST_ZERO.get(number_len, FIRST_ZERO_LONG)
                    else:
                        value = FIRST_OTHER.get(number_len, FIRST_OTHER_LONG)
                else:
                    after_zero = s[t - 1] == "0"
                    pair = SECOND_AFTER_ZERO if after_zero else SECOND_AFTER_OTHER
                    value = pair[0] if zero else pair[1]
                before = s[i] if i >= 0 else ""
                if before in DATA_LIKE:
                    value *= 0.5
                elif before in PROSE_LIKE or before == "" or _is_word(before):
                    value *= 1.4
    return None, float(value)

"""Selected non-English determiners and basic adjective forms.

Reassemble the current word and recognize grammatical word families in
Romance languages, German and Russian. Later pieces of a split spelling
usually get a larger response. Weak Slavic inflection cues fill in between
these lexical families. English adjective cognates need recent foreign
function words to receive the foreign-modifier response.

Japanese genitive marking and a standalone Chinese classifier have small
positive responses too. Small corrections cover English same/previous/following and initial letters.
State resets at document boundaries.
This is a word-form heuristic, not a full adjective or syntax recognizer.
"""
import codecs
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Patterns with responses for a word's first piece and for later pieces.
# These are translations/inflections of the named grammatical concepts.
FORMS = [
    # romance some any
    (r'(?:alg[uú]n[oa]?s?|algu(?:m|ns|ma|mas)|alcun[oaie]?|qualquer|'
     r'quaisquer|cualquier|cualesquiera|qualche|nenhum[ao]?s?|'
     r'ning[uú]n[oa]?s?|nessun[oaie]?)', 2.74, 5.2),
    # french indefinite
    (r'(?:quelques?|aucun[es]*|certain[es]*)', 1.98, 5.26),
    # romance other
    (r'(?:autres?|outr[oa]s?|otr[oa]s?|altr[oaie]|alt[aei])', 2.29, 4.55),
    # romance every
    (r'(?:chaque|chacun[e]?|ogni|tutt[oaie]|tod[oa]s?|cada)', 0.35, 0.92),

"""A local English object-noun-phrase detector.

Prepositions open a phrase; determiners and modifiers extend it. Dictionary
nouns receive a positive signal, especially in definite or possessive phrases.
Common nouns are weaker than rare ones. This is a rough grammar, not a parser:
only eight preceding words in the current clause are considered. There is also
an average negative document-start signal. Other scripts are mostly left near
zero; token-specific and longer-range variation is not modeled.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
PREPOSITIONS = set('''of in on at to from with for by under over into onto
through within around between during after before above below against without
across near behind toward towards upon beyond along about out off per via'''.split())
DEFINITE = set('the this that these those such'.split())
INDEFINITE = set('a an some any each every all both no many few several'.split())
POSSESSIVE = set('my your his her its our their whose'.split())
CLAUSE_WORDS = set('''i you he she it we they me him us them who which what
where when why how is are was were be been being am have has had do does did
can could will would shall should may might must not if because although
while as than then also there here'''.split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = (PREPOSITIONS | DEFINITE | INDEFINITE | POSSESSIVE
                  | CLAUSE_WORDS | {'and', 'or'})


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def parts(word):
    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def frequency(word):
    return zipf_frequency(word, 'en')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail = '' if first else carry[1]
    tail = (tail + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-180:]
    match = re.search(r"[A-Za-z]+(?:['’][A-Za-z]+)?$", tail)
    word = match[0].lower() if match else ''
    left = tail[:match.start()] if match else tail
    left = re.split(r'[.!?;:,(){}<>="`]|\n\n', left)[-1]
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+(?:['’][A-Za-z]+)?", left.lower())[-8:]

    role = 0.0
    depth = 0
    definite = possessive = False
    previous = ''
    for w in words:
        p = parts(w)
        if w in PREPOSITIONS:
            role, depth = 1.0, 0
            definite = possessive = False
        elif w in POSSESSIVE or w.endswith(("'s", '’s')):
            possessive, definite = True, False
            role, depth = max(role, 0.8), 0
        elif w in DEFINITE or w in INDEFINITE:
            if (role == 0 and previous and previous not in CLAUSE_WORDS
                    and 'verb' in parts(previous)):
                role = 0.4  # A possible direct object after a verb.
            definite, depth = w in DEFINITE, 0
        elif (w in CLAUSE_WORDS or
              ('verb' in p and not {'noun', 'adjective'} & p)):
            role, depth = 0.0, 0
            definite = possessive = False
        elif w not in {'and', 'or'}:
            depth += 1
            if depth > 5:
                role = 0.0
                definite = possessive = False
        previous = w

    p = parts(word) if word and word not in FUNCTION_WORDS else frozenset()
    value = -0.0046 - 0.3298 * first
    if 'noun' in p:
        value += role * (0.0965 + 0.0128 * min(depth, 3)
                         - 0.0155 * (frequency(word) - 4))
        value -= 0.0561 * possessive
        value += 0.0847 * (definite and role == 1)
        value += 0.1284 * (possessive and role == 1)
        value -= 0.0706 * (previous in PREPOSITIONS)
        value -= 0.0050 * (previous in DEFINITE)
    if 'adjective' in p:
        value -= 0.0049 * role
    if word and not {'noun', 'adjective', 'verb'} & p:
        value += 0.0268 * role
    if re.search(r'\d$', tail) and role > 0:
        value += 0.0547
    return (doc, tail), float(value)

wife son daughter parents child children horse fish dog cat bird tree plant leaf roots seed water air

DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789")

ZERO_STRENGTH = 0.6
WAIT_STRENGTH = 0.55


def zero_in_number(s, i):
    j = i
    while j > 0 and (s[j - 1] in DIGITS or s[j - 1] == "."):
        j -= 1

    after_point = i >= 2 and s[i - 1] == "." and s[i - 2] in DIGITS
    after_v = i >= 1 and s[i - 1].strip() == "v"

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:913 fires on the token "2" (also the subscript "₂"
and the Roman numeral " II") when it comes straight after a word: a Latin letter or
underscore that is part of a name, formula or identifier. It is quiet when the 2
begins a number ("2018", "in 2 hours"), weak after "-", "/" or "^", and near zero
when the preceding token is escaped or non-Latin text.

gets almost none. Each of these values was fit to the component's activations on
training text; the rule uses only the current token and the one before it.

ROMAN_VALUE = 0.75  # " II" or "II" right after a word, as in "World War II"
DASH_VALUE = 0.15  # "2" after "-", "/" or "^", as in HTTP/2
OTHER_VALUE = 0.05  # "2" after a digit, a space or punctuation (inside numbers)
TWO_VALUE = 0.1  # the word " two" and the superscript "²"
START_VALUE = -0.6  # a bare "2" that opens a document has no preceding token

    """True if the token ends in a plain Latin letter or underscore, and is not an escape."""
    return bool(text) and text.isascii() and (text[-1].isalpha() or text[-1] == "_") and "\\" not in text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else None
    if token == "2" and before is None:
        value = START_VALUE
    elif token in ("2", "₂") and ends_a_name(before):
        value = NAME_VALUE
    elif token in (" II", "II") and ends_a_name(before):
        value = ROMAN_VALUE
    elif token == "2" and before and before[-1] in "-/^":
        value = DASH_VALUE
    elif token == "2":
        value = OTHER_VALUE
    elif token in (" two", "²"):
        value = TWO_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, value

"""Detect the beginnings of modern years: 19... and 20....

Temporal words, months, citations and parentheses strengthen the response;
long numbers, arithmetic and decimal fractions weaken it. Separate rules
cover GitHub/GitLab hostnames and initial 'Title:' metadata.
Fullwidth digits are normalized, and Chinese 一九 is recognized too.
Only a short, document-local text suffix is retained; this is not a full
date parser. Other tokens receive zero.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
import regex

READS = ()
MONTHS = set('january february march april may june july august september '
             'october november december'.split())
MONTH_ABBREVIATIONS = set('jan feb mar apr jun jul aug sep sept oct nov dec'.split())
TIME_PREPOSITIONS = set('in since during from between until before after'.split())
PERIOD_WORDS = set('year years early late mid circa around'.split())
QUANTITY_WORDS = set('than about over under at approximately equals equal '
                     'exactly number numbers total'.split())


def year_value(token, previous):
    """Score a second century digit, using only the text before it."""
    m = re.search(r'[0-9]+$', previous)
    if not m:
        return 0.0
    number = m.group()
    if not ((number.endswith('1') and token == '9') or
            (number.endswith('2') and token == '0')):
        return 0.0
    old = token == '9'
    if len(number) > 1:
        return -0.05 if old else -0.43
    before = previous[:-1]
    trimmed = before.rstrip()
    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', before)
    word = words[-1] if words else ''
    lower = word.lower()
    if re.search(r'(?:copyright(?:\s*\(c\))?|©)[\d\s,–—-]*$',
                 before, re.IGNORECASE):
        return 2.55
    if lower == 'born' or (lower in MONTHS and
                           re.search(r'\bborn\b', before[-55:], re.IGNORECASE)):
        return 2.7
    citation = bool(re.search(r'\\cite\w*\{[^}]*$', before))

    # Add evidence for a year; subtract evidence for an ordinary quantity.
    value = 0.81 + 0.29 * old
    value += 1.03 * (lower in TIME_PREPOSITIONS)
    value += 0.45 * (lower in MONTHS)
    value -= 0.15 * (lower in MONTH_ABBREVIATIONS)
    value += 0.95 * (lower in PERIOD_WORDS or lower == 'the')
    value += 1.53 * (lower == 'al')
    value += 0.43 * trimmed.endswith(('(', '（'))
    value += 0.35 * (bool(word) and word[0].isupper())
    value += 0.57 * citation
    value -= 0.59 * (bool(re.search(r'[=+*^]|\\(?:frac|times)',
                                   before[-50:])) and not citation)
    value -= 0.56 * ('\t' in before[-20:] or before.endswith('  '))
    value -= 0.44 * (lower in QUANTITY_WORDS)
    value -= 0.19 * (bool(before) and before[-1].isascii()
                    and before[-1].isalpha())
    value += 0.69 * bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}$', trimmed))
    value += 0.79 * trimmed.endswith(('在', '于', '於', '自'))
    value -= 0.70 * bool(re.search(r'\d[.,]$', before))
    value -= 0.44 * bool(re.search(r'[$£€¥₹]\s*(?:\d+[.,])?\s*$', before))
    value -= 0.47 * bool(re.search(r'(?:19|20)\d{2}\s*[-–—/]\s*$', before))
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, count = '', 0
    else:
        _, previous, count = carry
    token = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = 0.0
    if token in {'0', '9'}:
        value = year_value(token, previous)
    elif token == 'Title' and count == 0:
        value = -1.04
    elif token == ':' and count == 1 and previous == 'Title':
        value = -20.65
    elif token == '.com':
        host = previous.lower()
        if host.endswith(('github', 'githubusercontent')):
            value = 3.3 if host.endswith('"github') else 2.6
        elif host.endswith('gitlab'):
            value = 1.1
    elif token == '九' and previous.rstrip().endswith('一'):
        digits = re.search(r'[〇零一二三四五六七八九]+$', previous)
        if digits and len(digits.group()) == 1:
            value = 4.2 if previous.endswith('在一') else 3.3
    return (doc, (previous + token)[-160:], count + 1), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:914 - a "start of a year" detector.

The component fires on the second digit of a number that begins a four-digit year,
i.e. the "9" of "19..." or the "0" of "20..." when the two digits open a number
(not the tail of a longer number). It is strongest when the text reads like dates or
biography ("in 19", "born 19", "March 19", "since 20"), and weak or absent in code,
line numbers, arithmetic and lists.

The program: at a "1" followed by "9", or a "2" followed by "0", that starts a number,
predict a value that is high in year-like prose and low elsewhere. It also gives a
moderate value (0.8) on a ".com" domain suffix, which the component also picks up.
"""

MONTHS = (
    "January February March April May June July August September October November "
    "December Jan Feb Mar Apr Jun Jul Aug Sep Sept Oct Nov Dec"
).split()
YEAR_WORDS = set("born died in since from until year founded established elected during circa".split())


READS = ()


def _year_cue(text):
    """True when the text just before the number reads like a date or a biography."""
    words = text.replace(",", " ").replace("(", " ").split()
    if not words:
        return False
    last = words[-1].lower()
    return last in YEAR_WORDS or any(word in MONTHS for word in words[-3:])

    tok = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    value = 0.0

        cur, prev, before = tok[-1], tok[-2], tok[-3]
        starts_number = not before.isdigit()
        if starts_number and ((prev == "1" and cur == "9") or (prev == "2" and cur == "0")):
            pre = prefix.text_prefixes[-3]
            value = 1.5 if cur == "9" else 0.8
            if _year_cue(pre[-40:]):
                value += 0.8
            if any(ch.isdigit() for ch in pre[-30:]):
                value -= 0.4

        value = 0.8

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 915: a whitespace-and-line-start reading.

In plain terms, it fires on indentation that does not come straight after a real
line break:
- Tab-plus-space indentation after a line-number prefix (listings like "  121<TAB>    x")
  fires, more strongly the deeper the indent (about 0.7 up to 1.2).
- Runs of spaces after a literal backslash-n (the two characters \\n in escaped code or
  text) fire at about 1.0, and so do tab runs of two or more after a line number.
- Indentation after a real newline is silent. So is almost all ordinary text.
- A lone space at the start of a line is negative (-0.75 after a newline, -1.1 after an
  escaped newline).
- The digit 1 that opens a numbered list item after a line break is mildly positive.
- The first token of a document (a row start or the token after <|endoftext|>) is
  mildly negative.

Predictions are 0 everywhere else, so the diffuse small activity on ordinary text is not modelled.
"""

READS = ()


def _is_ws(s):
    return s != "" and all(c in " \t\xa0" for c in s)


def _ends_escaped_newline(strings):
    # a literal backslash-n: the token "\\n", or a backslash token then "n"
    if not strings:
        return False
    last = strings[-1]
    if last == "\\n" or last.endswith("\\n"):
        return True
    return last == "n" and len(strings) > 1 and strings[-2].endswith("\\")


def _ends_real_newline(strings):
    return bool(strings) and "\n" in strings[-1] and "\\n" not in strings[-1]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    tok = strings[-1]
    prev = strings[:-1]
    # first token of a document (rows pack documents end to end)
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, -0.35
    if tok == "1" and _ends_real_newline(prev):
        return carry, 0.4
    if not _is_ws(tok):
        return carry, 0.0

    after_escape = _ends_escaped_newline(prev)
    after_newline = _ends_real_newline(prev)
    after_digit = bool(prev) and prev[-1].isdigit()
    tabs = tok.count("\t")
    spaces = tok.count(" ")

    if tabs and spaces:  # tab then spaces: indentation in a numbered listing
        if after_newline:
            return carry, 0.25
        return carry, 0.65 + 0.025 * min(spaces, 22)
    if tabs:
        if after_newline:
            return carry, 0.0
        if tabs >= 2:
            return carry, 0.9
        return carry, 0.2 if after_digit else 0.0
    if spaces >= 2:  # a run of spaces
        return carry, 1.0 if after_escape else 0.1
    # a lone space
    if after_newline:
        return carry, -0.75
    if after_escape:
        return carry, -1.1
    return carry, 0.0

    'a': 0.223,
    'e': -0.097,
    'i': 0.223,
    'o': -0.096,
    'u': 0.212,
    'y': 0.343,

    'ö': 0.631,

    if prev.strip() == 'e' and low == 'ing':

    return (doc, token, word, evidence, accent), float(value)

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 919: a weak, language-tilted fragment detector.

What the component does, as measured: it is almost always near zero. Its large activations
(|a| > 0.5 at about 0.03% of positions) sit on word-internal fragments: a token with no leading
space, made of letters, that continues a longer word split across tokens (e.g. "Kle|ink|unst",
"E|ing|ehend", "Vesitükim|aa"). The sign depends on the language being written. Inside German
text these fragments lean negative; inside Dutch or Finnish-like text they lean positive.

What this program does: it keeps a running tally of German versus Dutch function words in the
current document (decayed, reset at each new document). On a word-internal fragment it predicts
a small value with the sign of that tally: negative in German, positive in Dutch-like text.
Everywhere else it predicts 0.

This captures only a little of the variance (see the explanation); it is a readable summary of
the one regularity found, not a full model of the component.
"""

READS = ()

GERMAN = set("der und ist nicht mit das sich auf für ein eine dem den von zu auch werden wird sie aus bei ich wir".split())
DUTCH = set("het een en van niet op dat voor met zijn er ook aan naar maar bij deze wij zich".split())
DECAY = 0.98
SCALE = -0.0015  # predicted activation per unit of the tally, on fragments


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[1] != doc:
        tally = 0.0
    else:
        tally = carry[0]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = word.strip().lower()
    if core in GERMAN:
        tally += 1.0
    elif core in DUTCH:
        tally -= 1.0
    tally *= DECAY
    fragment = not word.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha()
    value = SCALE * tally if fragment else 0.0
    return (tally, doc), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 920: a "deny" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: this component writes a strong negative signal
whenever the word being typed is a form of the verb "to deny" or its noun
"denial": deny, denies, denied, denying, denial, denials, denier(s). The word
can be a single token (" denial", " denied") or spread over several byte-level
pieces ("Den" + "ial", "DEN" + "IED", "den" + "ied"); the signal lands on the
piece that completes the word, not on the earlier "den" piece (which stays
near zero). The name "Denis" (and the species author "Denis") gives a
somewhat weaker negative signal. Every other word, including other "den-"
words like dense, density, denominator, Denmark, denote, gets about zero.

How it works: the program keeps the word typed so far in its carry (the
letters since the last non-letter character, lowercased), and resets it at
a document boundary. At each token it appends the token's letters to the
word, then reads off the value from the word.

Activation scale: about -9.5 on deny-family words, -7 on "Denis", 0 elsewhere.
Measured on training rows this captures roughly half the variance (the
deny-family words carry about half of the component's sum of squares); the
remainder is a long tail of small, scattered values on word pieces starting
with "da"/"de" that no simple rule captures.
"""

READS = ()

# Forms of "deny" and "denial" and their typical activation (negative).
DENY_FORMS = frozenset({
    "deny", "denies", "denied", "denying",
    "denial", "denials", "denier", "deniers",
})
DENY_VALUE = -9.5

# The given name Denis (and the botanical/zoological author abbreviation).
NAME_FORMS = frozenset({"denis"})
NAME_VALUE = -7.0


def _tail_letters(text):
    """The trailing run of letters in text ("" if it ends in a non-letter)."""
    i = len(text)
    while i > 0 and text[i - 1].isalpha():
        i -= 1
    return text[i:]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The word typed so far, as a string; None at the start of a row.
    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""  # a new document starts a new word

    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if piece and all(c.isalpha() for c in piece):
        word = word + piece  # the token continues the current word
    else:
        word = _tail_letters(piece)  # the token ends the last word and may start a new one
    word = word[-24:]  # keep the carry small

    lower = word.lower()
    if lower in DENY_FORMS:
        value = DENY_VALUE
    elif lower in NAME_FORMS:
        value = NAME_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, float(value)

court metadata, generated Java idioms and decorative C comment headers.

    'name': (r' __$', 1.28),

    ' Date': (r'Decision$', -2.33),

    ' contributions': (r'\bAuthor$', -4.0),
    ' Contributions': (r'\bAuthor$', -3.3),

    'Points': (r'\n$', -3.2),

            if before.endswith((' Created', ' Updated')):

    return 0.0

    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:

    else:

    value = predict(token, before, previous)

5. Java: "@generated", and the method names "hashCode"/"toString" in overrides, are negative;

   "Court of" in legal text is mildly negative.

    "Page", "Question", "Problem", "Claim", "Claims", "Lemma", "Example", "Article",
    "Proposition", "Lesson", "Case", "Rule", "Line", "Definition", "Version", "Ratings",

    "Solution", "Answer", "Option", "Number",

    p = wordnet.parts_of_speech(w) if w.isascii() and w.isalpha() else ()
    return 'adverb' in p, 'noun' in p, 'verb' in p

@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def is_time(w):
    return 'noun.time' in wordnet.categories(w)


def token_class(w):
    if w in PREPS:
        return 'of' if w == 'of' else 'prep'

        return 'det'
    if w in COORD:
        return 'coord'
    if w in FUNCTION:

    if w == ',':

    if w in (')', ']', '）'):

    if adv and not ly and w not in FUNCTION | QUANT | PARTICLES:
        tags.append('adverb')
    if w in QUANT:
        tags.append('quant')
    if w in PARTICLES:
        tags.append('particle')
    if w == 'not':

    if w == ',':
        tags.append('after_comma')
    if w in (')', ']', '）'):

    if ASIDE_RE.search(low):
        phrase_tags.append('aside')
    if DEGREE_PHRASE.search(low):
        phrase_tags.append('degree_phrase')
    tm = TIME_PHRASE.search(low)

    fixed = []
    if low.endswith('without replacement') and cur == 'from':
        fixed.append('sampling_without_replacement')
    if w in DEGREE and cur == 'like':
        fixed.append('comparative_likeness')
    if w in DEGREE and cur == 'than':
        fixed.append('comparative_than')
    if w == 'only' and cur == 'the':
        fixed.append('only_definite')
    if ly and cur == 'speaking':
        fixed.append('adverbial_speaking')
    if w == 'or' and cur == 'else':
        fixed.append('or_else')
    if w == 'then' and cur == 'again':
        fixed.append('then_again')
    value += sum(FIXED.get(k, 0.0) for k in fixed)
    return state, float(value)

diagram), none for program, param, frame.

        tail = ""
    letters = "".join(c for c in s.lower() if c.isalpha())

    lead = s[:1] in " \t\n"

    "the and of is to a that with for on it as are be this was by from or an at which "
    "have not you we he they his her in".split()

    " In", "In", " IN", "-in", " en", " em", " в", " В", "В", " bei", " über", " unter",
    " till", " til", " à", " med",
}

# "at", "into" and weaker foreign counterparts.
AT_WORDS = {
    " at", " At", " into", " within", " im", " zu", " dans", " aus", " um", " op", " при", " из", " ut",
}

# Words that are also common in English; they count only in non-English text.

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings

Separated n/N gets a strong response, especially after a hyphen or in an
identifier. Word-internal n is weak, except at a lower-to-upper-case boundary.
Repetition adds a positive correction. Literal backslash-n escapes have a
separate repetition correction and an offset after another merged escape.
At document start, n, N and merged backslash-n instead get positive values.

Greek nu and Cyrillic en are normalized to n, with script-specific scaling.
Thai no-nu gets a negative value, weakened after a combining mark. Name-field
words get a smaller negative value. Other token-specific responses are omitted.

import re
import codecs
import unicodedata

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if first:
        carry = (doc, '', {}, 0, b'')
    _, prev, counts, escapes, pending = carry
    decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')('replace')
    decoder.setstate((pending, 0))
    original = decoder.decode(prefix.token_bytes[-1])
    pending = decoder.getstate()[0]
    s = original.translate(str.maketrans('νΝнН', 'nNnN'))
    strength = 0.3 if any(c in original for c in 'нН') else 1.0
    value = 0.0

    if s == '\\n' or (s == 'n' and prev.endswith('\\')):
        value = -0.82 + 0.19 * math.log1p(escapes)
        if prev == '\\n':
            value += 0.60
        escapes += 1
    elif (match := re.fullmatch(r'([\W_]*)([nN])', s)):
        punctuation, letter = match.groups()
        before = punctuation or prev
        if before[-1:].isalpha():
            if letter == 'N' and before[-1].islower():
                category, value = 'camel', -1.9
            else:
                category, value = 'suffix', -0.05
        elif before.endswith('-'):
            category = 'dash' + letter
            value = -2.55 if letter == 'n' else -1.65
        elif before.endswith('_'):
            category = 'underscore' + letter
            value = -1.4 if letter == 'n' else -2.3
        elif before.endswith("'") and letter == 'n':
            category, value = 'contraction', 0.0
        elif before.endswith('('):
            category = 'paren' + letter
            value = -1.5 if letter == 'n' else -1.3
        elif before.endswith(' '):
            category = 'space' + letter
            value = -1.7 if letter == 'n' else -1.4
        elif before.endswith('\n'):
            category, value = 'line' + letter, -1.7
        else:
            category, value = 'boundary' + letter, -1.15
        if category != 'suffix':
            repetition = counts.get(category, 0)
            rate = 0.7 if category == 'dashn' else 0.3
            value += rate * math.log1p(repetition)
            counts[category] = repetition + 1

            value *= 2.0

            value = 2.68 if letter == 'N' else 1.60
    elif s == 'น':

        after_mark = last and unicodedata.category(last).startswith('M')
        value = -0.15 if after_mark else -1.8

        value = -0.33

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:932: a weak, mostly-diffuse component with three readable effects.

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. JSON key quotes inside a tool call. Inside a <tool_call> block, the component goes
     strongly negative on the "{\"" that opens the call (the first key, "name"), mildly
     negative on "{\"" that opens a nested object, and negative on the opening quote of
     the next key after a comma (e.g. the `"arguments"` after `"name": "bash",`).
  2. The first token of a row, and the first token after a document break
     (<|endoftext|>): the component is mildly positive there, since the model has no
     context yet.
  3. The newline pair that closes an empty reasoning block: "</think>\\n\\n" gives a
     mildly negative value on the "\\n\\n".
Everywhere else it predicts 0. Most of the component's variance (about 80%) is small,
token-by-token noise that no simple rule captures, so this program explains only a
modest share of it.

Main program: runs `step` over a row, one token at a time, carrying the last few
characters of text and whether a tool call is open.
"""

READS = ()

TOOL_OPEN = "<tool_call>"
TOOL_CLOSE = "</tool_call>"
DOC_BREAK = "<|endoftext|>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tail, in_tool, prev = carry if carry is not None else ("", False, "")
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tail = (tail + tok)[-40:]
    if tail.endswith(TOOL_OPEN):
        in_tool = True
    if tail.endswith(TOOL_CLOSE):
        in_tool = False

    value = 0.0
    if prefix.position == 0 or prev == DOC_BREAK:
        value = 0.25  # start of a row or document: no context yet
    elif in_tool:
        if tok == '{"':
            value = -1.1  # opens the tool call's JSON, first key
        elif tok == ' {"':
            value = -0.4  # opens a nested object
        elif tok == ' "' and prev.endswith(","):
            value = -0.7  # opening quote of the next key
    elif tok == "\n\n" and tail.endswith("</think>\n\n"):
        value = -0.45  # blank line after an empty think block
    return (tail, in_tool, tok), value

"""Approximate a mathematical/numeric-continuation response.

The main negative responses are at spaces or TeX backslashes after operators,
and at 'q' completing a split geq/leq/neq command. Spacing, TeX context,
indentation and p-value notation adjust the strength. Byte-split thin spaces
are handled causally, starting with their possible UTF-8 prefix.

Number-bearing labels and months get weaker space responses. Two formatting
exceptions are paired middle dots (positive) and an initial // newline
(negative). Unmatched tokens get zero; smaller lexical effects are not modeled.
"""
import re
from calendar import month_name

READS = ()

RELATIONS = set('in notin to mapsto rightarrow leftarrow subset subseteq '
                'supset supset supseteq mid'.split())
ORDER = set('ge le geq leq ne neq'.split())
APPROXIMATE = set('sim approx equiv propto'.split())
BINARY_OPERATORS = set('times cdot otimes div pm mp cup cap'.split())
FORMATTING = set('big Big bigg Bigg large Large displaystyle textstyle '
            'scriptstyle scriptscriptstyle quad qquad'.split())
MONTHS = {name.lower() for name in month_name[1:]}
LABELS = set('figure fig section table chapter equation eq theorem lemma'.split())

# Columns: space, space-plus-backslash, backslash.
WEIGHTS = {
    'equals': (-0.27, -2.2, -3.0),
    'sign': (-0.25, -2.2, -2.65),
    'comparison': (-0.03, -2.4, -2.8),
    'compound operator': (-0.26, 0.0, 0.0),
    'other arithmetic': (0.22, 0.15, 0.08),
    'TeX relation': (-1.3, -2.8, -2.5),
    'TeX order': (-2.2, -2.5, -2.9),
    'TeX approximate': (-0.65, -1.9, -1.8),
    'TeX binary': (-0.8, -1.7, -1.8),
    'TeX formatting': (-0.25, -0.45, -0.65),
    'opening delimiter': (-0.08, -0.4, -0.15),
    'dollar': (-0.25, -0.35, -0.2),
    'month': (-0.13, 0.0, 0.0),
    'label': (-0.22, 0.0, 0.0),
    'range word': (-0.07, 0.0, 0.0),
    'other': (0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
}


def operator_group(previous, text):
    word = previous.strip()
    command = re.search(r'\\([A-Za-z]+)\Z', text)
    if command:
        name = command[1]
        if name in ORDER:
            return 'TeX order'
        if name in APPROXIMATE:
            return 'TeX approximate'
        if name in RELATIONS:
            return 'TeX relation'
        if name in BINARY_OPERATORS:
            return 'TeX binary'
        if name in FORMATTING:
            return 'TeX formatting'
    symbolic = bool(word) and not any(c.isalnum() for c in word)
    if symbolic and re.search(r'(==|!=|<=|>=|:=|\+=|-=)\Z', word):
        return 'compound operator'
    if symbolic and word.endswith('='):
        return 'equals'
    if symbolic and word.endswith(('+', '-', '−', '–', '±')):
        return 'sign'
    if symbolic and word.endswith(('<', '>', '≤', '≥', '∈', '∉', '→', '⇒')):
        return 'comparison'
    if symbolic and word.endswith(('×', '÷', '/', '*', '^')):
        return 'other arithmetic'
    if word in ('(', '[', '{'):
        return 'opening delimiter'
    if word.endswith('$'):
        return 'dollar'
    if word.lower() in MONTHS:
        return 'month'
    if word.lower().rstrip('.') in LABELS:
        return 'label'
    if word.lower() in ('to', 'than'):
        return 'range word'
    return 'other'


def predict(token, previous, text):
    if token == 'q' and re.search(r'\\(?:ge|le|ne)\Z', text):
        return -12.0
    if not previous and token == '//\n':
        return -3.03
    if token == '··':
        return 1.61
    if token not in (' ', ' \\', '\\'):
        return 0.0
    kind = (' ', ' \\', '\\').index(token)
    group = operator_group(previous, text)
    value = WEIGHTS[group][kind]
    if group in ('equals', 'sign', 'comparison', 'other arithmetic') and kind == 0:
        before = text[:-len(previous)] if previous else text
        value -= 0.58 * previous.startswith(' ')
        value -= 0.29 * ('$' in before or '\\' in before)
        value += 0.62 * text.split('\n')[-1].startswith(('  ', '\t'))
        if re.search(r'\bp\s*[*_]*\s*[<>]\Z', text, re.I):
            value -= 1.4
    if group == 'sign' and kind == 2:
        value = -4.1 if previous.startswith(' ') else -2.65
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, text, pending = '', '', 0.0
    else:
        _, previous, text, pending = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, previous, text)
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    # E2 80 begins thin spaces (and other U+2000..203F punctuation).
    # After a relation, predict the prefix and then any space continuation.
    next_pending = 0.0
    if raw == b'\xe2\x80' and re.search(r'[=+\-−±<>≤≥]\Z', text):
        value = -2.1 if text.endswith('>') else -4.0
        if re.search(r'\bp[^A-Za-z0-9]{0,8}[<>≤≥]\Z', text, re.I):
            value = -5.0
        next_pending = value
    elif pending and (b'\xe2\x80' + raw).decode('utf-8', 'replace').isspace():
        value = 0.57 * pending
    return (doc, token, (text + token)[-96:], next_pending), float(value)

The strongest written cues are Chinese 来/來 and their grass-radical
homophones 莱/萊. Compounds usually respond less, especially 'future'
and lexicalized words beginning with 来. English come inflections are
weaker. Lai/rai syllables in other scripts and across token boundaries
are additional cues, as are unfinished UTF-8 prefixes of 莱 and 原.
Small negative offsets mark document beginnings and end-of-text boundaries.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
import regex

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def lexical(text):
    s = text.strip()
    word = s.lower()
    if word in {'come', 'comes', 'came', 'cum'}:
        return 0.83 if word != 'cum' else 0.70
    if word == 'coming':
        return 0.27
    if s in {'莱', '萊'}:
        return 6.3 if s == '莱' else 8.0
    if '来' in s or '來' in s:
        traditional = '來' in s
        plain = s.replace('來', '来')
        if plain == '来':
            return 4.5 if traditional else 3.4
        if '未来' in plain or '越来越' in plain:
            return 0.60
        if plain in {'下来', '看来'}:  # come down / it seems
            return 5.1
        if plain == '来源':  # source / origin
            return 3.1
        if plain.endswith('来'):
            return 3.4 if traditional else 2.7
        if plain.endswith(('来的', '来了')):
            return 2.0
        if plain == '来看':
            return 1.8
        if plain.endswith('来说'):
            return 0.5
        return 0.0
    # Written syllables, not arbitrary Latin words ending in these letters.
    if regex.fullmatch(r'[\p{Hangul}\p{Katakana}]+', s):
        syllable = anyascii(s).lower()
        if syllable == 'lae':
            return 2.75
        if syllable in {'lai', 'rai'}:
            return 1.9
    if word in {'lai', 'lại'}:  # romanized Lai; Vietnamese 'again'
        return 1.8
    if s == 'มา':  # Thai: come
        return 1.6
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = (len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or
             prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2])
    value = lexical(text)
    if first:
        return None, value - 0.20

    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    # A split romanized LAI, or Vietnamese lá + i.
    tail = anyascii(previous).lower()
    if ((text == 'ai' and tail.endswith('l')) or
            (text == 'i' and tail.endswith('la'))):
        value = 3.5
    # The second half of Chinese 'source' (来源), when split.
    elif text == '源' and previous in {'来', '來'}:
        value = 3.2
    # Ambiguous, unfinished UTF-8 prefixes shared with 莱 and 原.
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    if raw == b'\x8e':
        pair = prefix.token_bytes[-2][-1:] + raw
        if pair == '莱'.encode('utf-8')[:2]:
            value = 5.5
        elif pair == '原'.encode('utf-8')[:2]:
            value = 2.7
    if previous == '<|endoftext|>':
        value -= 0.12
    return None, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 935: a "come" / "lai" detector.

It fires on the word that means *come* (or the sound *lai*) at the token itself,
with no need to look at earlier tokens beyond one for the split "l" + "ai" case:

- Chinese 來 / 萊 standing alone (the verb 'to come', or a name): strong, about 4.8.
- Chinese 来 / 莱 / Korean 래 standing alone: about 3.5.
- A compound ending in 来/來 where the word is a 'come' verb complement
  (下来, 出来, 起来, 看来, 传来): about 2.6. A compound that starts with 来
  (来说, 来源, 来自, 来到) carries the sound but not the verb: about 0.4.
  未来 (future) is the exception at 0.7.
- Other 'lai' sounds: 라이 and ライ about 3, Vietnamese lại about 1.8.
- English 'come', 'came', 'comes' about 0.8 and 'coming' about 0.4.
- 'ai' right after a token ending in 'l' (Nikolai, Palaiologos, Nil-ai): about 2.7.
- Everything else: 0.

a signed contribution, and the program only predicts the common positive cases.
"""
READS = ()
STRONG = set("來萊")
PLAIN = set("来莱래")

        return carry, 4.8
    if tok in PLAIN:
        return carry, 3.5

        return carry, 0.7

        if tok[-1] in "来來":
            return carry, 2.6
        return carry, 0.4

        return carry, 0.8
    if s == "coming":

"""Dictionary keys: the quote that opens a key in a key-value literal.

Component 936 of the layer-1 MLP down projection of Qwen3-1.7B. It fires on the
opening quote mark of a KEY in a dictionary or JSON object (or a PHP / Ruby style
`'key' => value` array): the `"` or `'` that starts the next key after a comma or
a new line. Examples: the `"arguments"` in a tool call
`{"name": "bash", "arguments": {...}}`, or `'age'` in
`{'name': 'John', 'age': 30}`.
It stays silent on a quote that opens a value (the quote after a colon or arrow),
and is weaker for quoted items in a plain list. It also fires on the `(` that opens
the condition of an `if`, `for`, `while` or `switch`.

The program keeps a stack of open brackets (reset at each new document). For each
bracket it notes whether a colon or an arrow has appeared inside it, which tells a
key-value literal from a plain list.
"""

READS = ()

QUOTES = {' "', " '", '"', "'"}
# a closing quote, a comma and the next key's opening quote, in one token
MERGED_KEY_STARTS = {'","', "','"}
CONDITION_WORDS = {'if', 'for', 'while', 'switch', 'catch', 'foreach', 'elif'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    cur = prefix.token_strings[t]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[t - 1] if t > 0 else ''
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    stack = [] if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    # innermost open bracket: [char, key-value literal?]; '' when none is open
    top = stack[-1] if stack else ['', False]
    value = 0.0
    if cur in QUOTES or cur in MERGED_KEY_STARTS:
        before = prev.rstrip(' \n\t')
        recent = ''.join(prefix.token_strings[max(0, t - 12):t])
        has_colon_nearby = ':' in recent
        after_comma = before.endswith(',') or cur in MERGED_KEY_STARTS
        new_line = prev.strip() == ''
        if top[1]:  # inside a key-value literal
            if after_comma:
                value = 3.1 if top[0] == '{' else 1.9
            elif new_line:
                value = 1.4 if top[0] == '{' else 2.2
        elif top[0] == '{' and after_comma:
            value = 1.1
        elif not top[0] and after_comma and has_colon_nearby:
            value = 2.5
    elif cur.lstrip() in ('(', '(!', '($', '(int') and prev.strip() in CONDITION_WORDS:
        value = 1.3

    for ch in cur:
        if ch in '{([':
            stack.append([ch, False])
        elif ch in '})]':
            if stack:
                stack.pop()
    if stack and (':' in cur or '=>' in cur):
        stack[-1][1] = True
    return stack, value

"""Detect all-capital emphasis against a lower-case background.

Dictionary word frequency and grammatical classes approximate the distinction
between ordinary English words and abbreviations. Negation, quantifiers and
auxiliaries have stronger responses. The lower-case letter fraction over the
last forty tokens, raised to the fourth power, suppresses uniformly capitalized passages.
A preceding lower-case token strengthens the response further.
The same capitalization context is retained through a split word.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
from wordnet import parts_of_speech

READS = ()
PERSONAL_WORDS = set(
    'i you he she it we they me him her us them my your his its our their '
    'mine yours ours theirs'.split())
NEGATION = set('not no never neither nor nothing nobody nowhere none'.split())
AUXILIARIES = set(
    'be am is are was were been being have has had do does did can could '
    'may might shall should will would must don doesn didn won wouldn '
    'couldn shouldn isn aren wasn weren'.split())
DETERMINERS = set(
    'a an the this that these those some any all each every both either '
    'much many few more most less least other another same such only own'.split())
CONJUNCTIONS = set('and or but so yet for if then than because although while as'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = set(
    'of to in on at from by with about into over under out up down off per '
    'via between through before after'.split())
GRAMMAR = (
    (PERSONAL_WORDS, 0.72), (NEGATION, 4.65), (AUXILIARIES, 2.25),
    (DETERMINERS, 3.65), (CONJUNCTIONS, 2.15), (PREPOSITIONS, 1.85),
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def lexical(word):
    return zipf_frequency(word, 'en'), parts_of_speech(word)


def lower_share(tokens):
    text = ''.join(tokens)
    return sum(c.islower() for c in text) / max(
        1, sum(c.isalpha() for c in text))


def strength(piece, whole):
    frequency, pos = lexical(piece)
    full_frequency, _ = lexical(whole)
    value = 0.1 if len(piece) > 1 and full_frequency > 3.1 else 0.0
    if len(whole) > 2 and full_frequency > 5.6:
        value = 1.3
    if len(piece) > 2:
        if frequency > 4.5 and (('adjective' in pos) or ('verb' in pos)):
            value = 0.65
        if 'adverb' in pos and frequency > 4.9:
            value = 2.75 if frequency > 5.6 else 1.75
        for words, response in GRAMMAR:
            if piece in words:
                return response
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        history, word, word_context = (), '', 0.0
    else:
        _, history, word, word_context = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = history[-1] if history else ''
    continuing = bool(word) and s[:1].isalpha()
    if not continuing:
        preceding = 1.0 if lower_share((previous,)) > 0.25 else 0.2
        word_context = lower_share(history) ** 4 * preceding
    word = word + s if continuing else s.lstrip()
    word = re.split(r'[^\w\']', word)[-1][-40:]
    letters = ''.join(c for c in s if c.isalpha())
    value = 0.0
    if s.isupper() and len(word) > 1 and letters:
        value = strength(letters.lower(), word.lower())
        if word.isupper():
            value = max(value, strength(word.lower(), word.lower()))
        if not letters.isascii():
            value = 0.7
        value *= word_context
    return (doc, (*history[-39:], s), word, word_context), value

"""Approximate a line-ending feature from line length and formatting.

The main response is negative for lines about 20--60 tokens long, and
weaker for shorter or much longer lines. Character density, numeric
content, math delimiters, and punctuation adjust that response. Actual
newlines and written backslash-n escapes both end a logical line.

from bisect import bisect_right
from math import exp, log1p

READS = ()

LENGTHS = (0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 20, 32, 48, 80, 128, 256, 512)
RESPONSE = (-.060, .119, .107, .019, -.170, -.639,
            -.971, -.949, -.665, -.448, -.206, -.313)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, None, '', '', 0)
    _, position, last_break, previous, line, previous_length = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    escaped = '\\n' in token or (token == 'n' and previous.endswith('\\'))
    if '\n' not in token and not escaped:
        return (doc, position + 1, last_break, token,
                line + token, previous_length), -0.002

    length = position if last_break is None else position - last_break - 1
    k = min(bisect_right(LENGTHS, length) - 1, len(LENGTHS) - 2)
    f = (length - LENGTHS[k]) / (LENGTHS[k + 1] - LENGTHS[k])
    value = RESPONSE[k] * (1 - f) + RESPONSE[k + 1] * f

    # Line content counts refer to tokens preceding this line-ending token.
    chars = len(line)
    digit_fraction = sum(c.isdigit() for c in line) / max(chars, 1)
    value += .089 * min(chars, 300) / 100
    value -= .181 * min(chars / max(length, 1), 12) / 5
    value += .767 * digit_fraction
    value -= .288 * digit_fraction * min(chars, 300) / 20
    value -= .083 * exp(-previous_length / 12)
    value += .218 * log1p(position) / 6 - .062 * exp(-position / 24)
    if last_break is None:
        value -= .050

    # Local formatting of the line ending.
    if token.count('\n') >= 2:
        value += .071
    if token.count('\n') >= 3:
        value += .094
    if '\t' in token:
        value += .569
    if any(c in token for c in '{}'):
        value -= .164
    if any(c in token for c in '\'"'):
        value -= .129
    if '`' in token:
        value -= .133
    if escaped:
        value -= .062
    if '...' in token or '…' in token:
        value -= .373
    ending = line + token.split('\n')[0].split('\\n')[0]
    if ending.rstrip().endswith(('$', '\\]')):
        value += .585
    return (doc, position + 1, position, token, '', length), value

"""A partial lexical/contextual approximation, chiefly for Chinese.

Enumeration endings and labels of diverse collections get negative values;
consecutive, continuing and recurring actions get positive values. Smaller
rules cover initiative, lower bounds, married pairs, and no-cost offers.
Traditional spelling is normalized, and split words can use preceding text.
The first token has a separate correction because its responses differ
from the same token in running text. This does not reconstruct the MLP.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import cedict
from opencc import OpenCC

READS = ()
_SIMPLIFY = OpenCC('t2s')

# Semantically named word classes, not tokenizer IDs.
WORD_CLASSES = (
    (3.02, set('连续 轮流'.split())),               # consecutive / taking turns
    (0.94, set('继续 持续 始终 陆续 接连 先后 尽量'.split())),
    (0.55, set(
        '一直 总是 永远 天天 每天 依旧 坚持 重复 一律 全程'.split()
    )),
    (0.69, set('主动 单独 独自 自愿 自主'.split())), # initiative / independence
    (1.07, set('至少 最少'.split())),              # lower bounds
)
DOMAINS = set('领域 方面 环节 部位 步骤 场所 工序 学科 行业'.split())
DETAILS = set(
    '信息 知识 理论 优点 特点 问题 因素 内容 政策 规定 功能 工作 '
    '条件 情况 原因 形式 手段 事项 事宜'.split()
)
OFFICES = set('部门 组织 机构 单位 企业 负责人 责任人 同志'.split())
PLACES = set('国 国家 省 省份 省市 地区 城市'.split())
LABELS = DOMAINS | DETAILS | OFFICES | PLACES
FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    '的 地 得 和 与 及 或 了 是 为 在 对 也 都 将 有 还 就 更 而 但 '
    '不 可 可以 到 来 中 上 下 时 以 把 被'.split()
)
QUALIFIER = re.compile(
    r'(各|多个|各个|各类|各项|各种|不同|其他|其它|这些|那些|诸|多|'
    r'一些|许多|几个|相关|有关|个|种|名|位|家)$'
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def normalize(text):
    return _SIMPLIFY.convert(text.strip())

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def enumeration_compound(s):
    # Dictionary words such as 等待 (wait) and 等于 (equal) are not lists.
    return (s.startswith('等') and len(s) > 1
            and not any(cedict.glosses(s[:i]) for i in range(2, len(s)+1)))


def lexical_value(text, previous):
    s = normalize(text)
    value = -0.002
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Han}+', s):
        value -= 0.003
        for strength, words in WORD_CLASSES:
            if s in words or any(
                len(s) < len(w) and w.endswith(s)
                and previous.endswith(w[:-len(s)]) for w in words
            ):
                value += strength
        if s == '免费' or (s == '费' and previous.endswith('免')):
            value += 1.71 if s == text.strip() else 1.18
        if s in {'夫妻', '夫妇'}: value += 1.21
        if s in DOMAINS: value -= 0.37
        if s in DETAILS: value -= 0.03
        if s in OFFICES: value -= 0.13
        if s in PLACES: value -= 0.16
        if s == '国家': value -= 0.73
        if '不同' in s: value -= 0.53 if s.endswith('的') else 1.05
        if re.match(r'多[人名位家次个地国]', s): value -= 0.96
        if re.match(r'各[地国界省部门]', s): value -= 1.48
        if re.match(r'(各[个项种级]|多种)', s): value -= 0.18
        if re.match(r'(相关|有关).+', s): value -= 0.81
        if enumeration_compound(s):
            value -= 2.53
            if s.endswith('的'): value += 0.17
            if s in {'等人', '等多种', '等一系列', '等各种'}: value += 1.23
        elif s not in FUNCTION_WORDS and s != '等':
            if previous.endswith('等'):
                value -= 0.40
                if s in LABELS: value -= 1.59
            elif re.search(r'等(?:相关|各个|有关|多个)$', previous):
                value -= 1.44
        if s in LABELS:
            if QUALIFIER.search(previous): value -= 0.65
            if s in PLACES and re.search(
                r'(各|多|个|其他|其它|这些|那些|许多)$', previous
            ):
                value -= 0.61
        if s.endswith('国家') and len(s) > 2: value -= 1.68
    if text.startswith('など') and len(text) > 2:  # Japanese "etc."
        value -= 0.79 if text == 'などで' else 0.47
    if s and set(s) == {'·'} and len(s) > 1: value -= 0.42
    if text == '://': value -= 0.14
    return value


# Closed-class English reference words: pronouns and determiners.
REFERENCE_WORDS = set(
    'i me we us you he him she her it they them my your his its our their '
    'this that these those a an the each every some any no both either neither '
    'another such what which who whose'.split()
)


def first_token_correction(text):
    s = text.strip()
    if text.startswith('<|') or text.startswith('</') or text.startswith('<think'):
        return -0.20
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', s): return 0.0
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Hangul}', s): return 0.13
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Cyrillic}', s): return -0.24
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Arabic}', s): return -0.25
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Hiragana}|\p{Script=Katakana}', s):
        return -0.05
    if text.isspace(): return -0.30
    if s.isdigit(): return -0.28
    if s.lower() in REFERENCE_WORDS: return -0.55
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{P}+', s): return -0.15
    if s.isalpha(): return -0.08
    return -0.06


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = lexical_value(text, previous)
    if first:
        value += first_token_correction(text)
        # Escaped indentation, byte escapes, and code headers at a row start.
        if text == r'\t': value = 2.32
        elif text == r'\xc': value = 1.25
        elif text == '.\\': value = 2.54
        elif text == '///': value = 1.77
        elif text == '__': value = -1.73
    return (doc, (previous + normalize(text))[-24:]), float(value)
